transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

The display retaining the time while heating stops, then restarting after opening and shutting the door, most points to an intermittent door-interlock/latch connection. Grease or debris in the latch slots, worn door hooks or alignment can cause it; if those are all sound, the internal interlock microswitches or their mechanism are more likely. With it unplugged, wipe the door hooks and their receiving slots clean and inspect for cracking or damage; do not remove the casing or attempt internal microwave repairs. If the door feels normal and this continues, arrange a microwave engineer—an intermittent door safety circuit is not a fault to leave developing. Does the door latch firmly and evenly, or does it need pressure/lifting to keep it running?

It latches normally, no pressure needed. I cleaned some grease from the door hooks and latch slots and it's still happened once since. The handle side looks very slightly lower, but I can't be sure. No smell, sparks or tripping.

The most likely fault is now an intermittent internal door-interlock microswitch or its latch mechanism. The slight possible drop on the handle side could contribute through alignment, but it is not enough on its own to prove a hinge fault. This is not an internal repair to attempt on a microwave: arrange a microwave engineer to inspect the door alignment, latch mechanism and interlock switches, and avoid leaving it running unattended meanwhile. If it always stops only after several minutes, a cooling fan/thermal cut-out becomes more plausible; if it is genuinely random, especially early in a run, that strengthens the interlock diagnosis.

candidates: Intermittent door interlock switch or door latch engagement (high)
Door hooks/slots contaminated or slightly misaligned (medium)
